package main

import (
	"encoding/json"
	"encoding/xml"
	"fmt"
)

// Record nests interpreter-owned slices inside a local struct. The read-only
// marshalers must walk the transported value tree and allocate their own
// output without retaining or mutating those slices.
type Record struct {
	Name   string   `json:"name" xml:"name"`
	Tags   []string `json:"tags" xml:"tag"`
	Scores []int    `json:"scores" xml:"score"`
}

func main() {
	r := Record{Name: "widget", Tags: []string{"a", "b", "c"}, Scores: []int{3, 1, 2}}
	j, err := json.Marshal(r)
	fmt.Println("json:", string(j), err)
	x, err := xml.Marshal(r)
	fmt.Println("xml:", string(x), err)
	// A bare slice argument, not nested in a struct.
	nums, _ := json.Marshal([]int{9, 8, 7})
	fmt.Println("nums:", string(nums))
	// The originals are unchanged and still usable after marshaling.
	fmt.Println("after:", r.Tags, r.Scores)
}
